item.description:
On December 10, 1986, I was 14 years old, sitting in Oslo City Hall as my father, Elie Wiesel, accepted the Nobel Peace Prize. I will never forget the look of hope on his face that day. He had spent his life tortured by the thought that the world had looked away from the Jewish people as the Nazis filled the gas chambers and crematoria with our brothers and sisters, aunts and uncles, children. Finally, he felt seen, and he had a message to share. As he put it in his acceptance speech, “We must always take sides. Neutrality helps the oppressor, never the victim.” My father was honored because he had turned the memory of genocide into a moral duty to the living. item.title: Prediction Markets Have a Lock on the Midterms
item.description:
As so-called prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket embed themselves in every aspect of our daily lives, from elections to sports and entertainment, concerns have grown about what the explosion of these poorly understood, loosely regulated platforms could mean for regular people and democracy writ large. Celebrities from LeBron James to Sydney Sweeney have inked lucrative deals with prediction platforms. Legacy news outlets have even begun including prediction market data in their coverage. And the Trump family is deeply embedded in these platforms’ success; Donald Trump Jr.’s VC firm just became a lead investor in Polymarket, and he is a paid adviser to both Polymarket and Kalshi. But what actually is a prediction market, and what separates it from online sports betting platforms like DraftKings or FanDuel? item.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens as it heads towards land
item.description:
The hurricane approaching the northern Gulf Coast has been upgraded to a major Category 3 with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph — and it threatens to bring heavy rain, severe flooding, tornadoes, and power outages to the western Florida Panhandle, Alabama, Mississippi, and other parts of the Southeast. Hurricane Isaias, the first of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, is set to make landfall near the Pensacola, Florida, area Friday evening with a life-threatening storm surge of up to 9 feet. Coastal Alabama to Port St. Joe could also see 5 to 7 feet. Forecasters expect some weakening before the hurricane hits land, but warn Isaias will remain dangerous regardless of its exact strength. Mandatory evacuation orders have been issued for several coastal counties. item.title: Anne Carson and the Beauty of the Unsaid
item.description:
This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. The literature of ancient Greece and Rome seems to be in vogue. This summer, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey turned Homer’s epic poems into best sellers, and yesterday the Nobel Prize was awarded to Anne Carson, a poet who has made a career of repurposing ancient-Greek works. Perhaps this resurgence has something to do with modern anxieties about the future; people tend to look back to the past in uncertain times. Although I’m glad to see the classics prominently displayed in bookstores, I’m not convinced that they hold a special kind of wisdom that contemporary writing can’t access.
